Same as above, but the overall mean is computed over all Examination rows with non-null `aCL IgM` before the join, so examinations without a matching patient still count toward the mean.

Patient-level: collapse to one entry per patient `ID` (average `aCL IgM` across their examinations), then compute the overall mean as the average of the per-patient values, deviations, per-sex averages and top 10.
Patient-level with the overall mean still taken over examination rows (each patient weighted by their number of examinations), but entries listed once per patient.

Rows with NULL `aCL IgM` are kept in the ranking with NULL deviation and NULL excess, placed last, if fewer than 10 rows qualify.
Rows whose `SEX` is NULL are excluded because they match no sex group (their sex average is NULL).
Rows whose `SEX` is NULL are shown with NULL excess and ranked last.
Rows whose `SEX` is an empty or blank string form their own group with its own average deviation and may appear in the results.
"Exceeds" means strictly greater than (deviation > sex average deviation).
"Exceeds" means greater than or equal to (deviation ≥ sex average deviation).
Ties at the 10th position are cut arbitrarily by the LIMIT 10.
Ties at the 10th position are all included, which may return more than 10 rows.
Ties are broken by `ID` or `Examination Date` for a deterministic order.

The output has one row per examination, so the same patient `ID` can appear multiple times with different `aCL IgM` values.
The output keeps only each patient's highest-ranked examination (one row per `ID`).
The sex average is computed across all non-null rows in the sex group, including rows that are later filtered out, so the filter and the average use the same population.

queries:
WITH j AS (
    SELECT e.ID AS ID, e.`aCL IgM` AS igm, p.SEX AS SEX
    FROM Examination e
    JOIN Patient p ON e.ID = p.ID
    WHERE e.`aCL IgM` IS NOT NULL
),
d AS (
    SELECT ID, SEX, igm - (SELECT AVG(igm) FROM j) AS dev
    FROM j
),
s AS (
    SELECT SEX, AVG(dev) AS avgdev
    FROM d
    GROUP BY SEX
)
SELECT d.ID
FROM d
JOIN s ON d.SEX = s.SEX
WHERE d.dev > s.avgdev
ORDER BY d.dev - s.avgdev DESC
LIMIT 10;
SELECT COUNT(T1.ID) FROM Patient AS T1 INNER JOIN Examination AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID WHERE T1.Admission = '-' AND T2.`aCL IgM` > (SELECT AVG(`aCL IgM`) * 1.2 FROM Examination WHERE `aCL IgM` IS NOT NULL);
WITH per_patient AS (
    SELECT e.ID, p.SEX, AVG(e."aCL IgM") AS avg_igm
    FROM Examination e
    JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = e.ID
    WHERE e."aCL IgM" IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY e.ID, p.SEX
),
overall AS (
    SELECT AVG(avg_igm) AS overall_mean FROM per_patient
),
sex_avg AS (
    SELECT SEX, AVG(avg_igm) AS sex_mean FROM per_patient GROUP BY SEX
)
SELECT pp.ID,
       pp.SEX,
       pp.avg_igm,
       o.overall_mean,
       pp.avg_igm - o.overall_mean AS deviation,
       s.sex_mean
FROM per_patient pp
CROSS JOIN overall o
JOIN sex_avg s ON s.SEX = pp.SEX
ORDER BY pp.avg_igm DESC
LIMIT 10;
SELECT e.ID
FROM Examination e
JOIN Patient p ON e.ID = p.ID
WHERE e.`aCL IgM` IS NOT NULL
  AND e.`aCL IgM` > (
    SELECT AVG(e2.`aCL IgM`)
    FROM Examination e2
    JOIN Patient p2 ON e2.ID = p2.ID
    WHERE p2.SEX = p.SEX
  );
